title: Received purchase order lines and accepted vendor bills keep the old number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test.
  • Create a purchase order for this test, purchase order 1, from any vendor, with a line for part A picked from the lookup, 1 ordered and fully received on a vendor invoice.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  6. Open purchase order 1.
  7. Click Vendor Invoices in the left menu.
  8. Open the vendor invoice of purchase order 1's receipt.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved, the window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 5:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • Purchase order 1's fully received line still reads the old number: completed records keep their number.

Step 7:

  • The Vendor Invoices list opens.

Step 8:

  • The accepted vendor invoice still reads the old number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19b: “Vendor bills already accepted keep the number they were written with.”
  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: S13-R19 matters because those records hold their own copy of the number and find the part by it later. Records already completed, such as received purchase order lines, completed returns and past work orders and invoices, keep the number they were written with. The Inventory list, Part History, Parts Velocity and today's Inventory Value show the new number. Inventory Value run for a date before the rename shows the number as it was on that date.”
  • Key Decisions: “A rename carries over to work that is still open. Open purchase order lines, open part requests, canned jobs and open returns follow the new number, so receiving and returning still find the part. Records already completed keep the number they were written with.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
